note: Blind ground-truth rehearsal scripts. The pipeline receives only turn text/audio; expected_stems are harness-only grading keys and must never be sent to the service.

interviews.focus: Warmup grounded in DriveWealth's platform basics

turns.text: You have read about our platform. In one minute, what is DriveWealth's business and where would AI agents plausibly fit?
turns.expected_stems: drivewealth business ai agents fit brokerage

turns.text: What is an agent to you, and how is that different from a single model call answering a partner support ticket?
turns.expected_stems: agent different single model call partner support

turns.text: Our partners integrate against our Investing API. What state would an agent keep while helping a partner through account opening?
turns.expected_stems: partners investing api state agent account opening

turns.text: How do you stop an agent from retrying a failed deposit call forever?
turns.expected_stems: stop retrying failed deposit forever limit

turns.text: What do you log on every agent run at minimum, in a company regulated by FINRA?
turns.expected_stems: log every run minimum regulated finra

turns.text: How do you test an agent that talks to our sandbox environment, given the sandbox mirrors production?
turns.expected_stems: test agent sandbox environment mirrors production

turns.text: Explain retrieval augmented generation using our developer documentation as the corpus in your example.
turns.expected_stems: retrieval augmented generation developer documentation corpus

turns.text: What makes an agent's answer trustworthy enough to show one of our partners' customers?
turns.expected_stems: answer trustworthy partners customers grounded

playback.note: voice the question, then hold a 60s answer pause; continuous piece

interviews.focus: Platform/SDK design and observability with fintech flavor

turns.text: We run a regulated brokerage platform. If our internal teams want to build agents on top of our order and account APIs, what does the shared agent platform you would build for them look like?
turns.expected_stems: regulated brokerage internal teams agents platform order account apis

turns.text: Our services publish account and order events onto SQS queues. How would an agent system consume those events safely, and what happens when a consumer falls behind or an event arrives twice?
turns.expected_stems: sqs queues events consume safely behind twice idempotent

turns.text: How do you version the tools you expose to agents so that a tool change cannot silently break twenty workflows owned by other teams?
turns.expected_stems: version tools change silently break workflows teams

turns.text: A junior engineer ships an agent that calls our trading API. What guardrails does your platform put between that agent and a live order endpoint?
turns.expected_stems: junior guardrails agent trading api live order

turns.text: What does your tracing look like for one agent run that spans retrieval, three tool calls, and two model calls? What triggers an alert?
turns.expected_stems: tracing run retrieval tool calls model alert

turns.text: Customer PII flows through KYC documents like W-8 and W-9 forms. How do you keep that data out of prompts, logs and traces programmatically?
turns.expected_stems: pii kyc documents prompts logs traces programmatically

turns.text: How do you measure retrieval precision for an internal knowledge assistant, and what number would make you stop a rollout?
turns.expected_stems: measure retrieval precision knowledge assistant stop rollout

turns.text: Compliance asks you to prove what an agent did on a specific customer account three weeks ago. Walk me through how your system answers that.
turns.expected_stems: compliance prove agent customer account weeks audit

playback.note: voice the question, then hold a 60s answer pause; continuous piece

interviews.focus: Live system design under regulatory constraints, deep failure handling

turns.text: Design this live with me. We want an agent system that reconciles failed or stuck orders across our clearing pipeline overnight and proposes corrective actions for a human ops team each morning. Sketch the architecture.
turns.expected_stems: reconciles failed stuck orders clearing overnight corrective human ops architecture

turns.text: In that reconciliation system, an agent concludes an order needs to be cancelled and rebooked. Nobody should trust that conclusion blindly. Where exactly does verification live, and what does the human approve?
turns.expected_stems: cancelled rebooked trust conclusion verification human approve

turns.text: Now scale it. Ten thousand accounts, bursty SQS event volume, model provider rate limits, and a hard morning deadline. What breaks first and how does the design absorb it?
turns.expected_stems: scale accounts bursty volume rate limits deadline breaks absorb

turns.text: Your agent recommends portfolio rebalances in an advisory product. A regulator asks how you ensure a hallucinated fact can never reach a customer recommendation. What is the actual mechanism?
turns.expected_stems: rebalances advisory regulator hallucinated fact customer recommendation mechanism

turns.text: One of the agents in production starts disagreeing with the deterministic reconciliation numbers on Tuesday morning. Show me your first fifteen minutes of diagnosis.
turns.expected_stems: disagreeing deterministic reconciliation tuesday diagnosis fifteen minutes

turns.text: We prefer the AWS Strands SDK but stay open to LangGraph. Argue for the orchestration approach you would actually bring here, against your own preference where honest.
turns.expected_stems: strands langgraph orchestration approach argue preference

turns.text: Suppose I hand you a broken agent right now: it loops, burns tokens, and returns nothing. You have my screen. What do you type first?
turns.expected_stems: broken agent loops burns tokens returns nothing type first

turns.text: Last question. Your platform is live, adopted by five teams. What is the first standard you enforce ruthlessly and the first one you deliberately relax?
turns.expected_stems: standard enforce ruthlessly deliberately relax

playback.note: voice the question, then hold a 60s answer pause; continuous piece

interviews.focus: Questions asked at the level of DriveWealth's actual API spec, SQS topics, and infra

turns.text: You have seen our developer docs. Our partners create users, run KYC, open accounts, fund them, and place orders through our Investing API. Where in that lifecycle would an agent add real value first, and why there?
turns.expected_stems: partners users kyc accounts fund orders lifecycle agent value first

turns.text: Our autopilot endpoints run managed rebalances, and each rebalance run has an identifier and a lifecycle. If an agent monitored rebalance runs, what state would it keep per run and what would it never be allowed to do?
turns.expected_stems: autopilot managed rebalances identifier lifecycle state never allowed

turns.text: We publish order and account events to partner SQS queues. Partners constantly mishandle redeliveries and out of order events. Design the consumer you would give them as a platform primitive.
turns.expected_stems: order account events sqs redeliveries order consumer platform primitive

turns.text: A deposit fails after the redemption side already settled. An agent notices the mismatch in the funding events. What does it do in the next sixty seconds, and what does it absolutely not do?
turns.expected_stems: deposit fails redemption settled mismatch funding sixty seconds not

turns.text: Our sandbox is a production replica selected by hostname. How would your agent platform use that environment in its release process, and what can a sandbox pass never prove?
turns.expected_stems: sandbox production replica hostname release process pass never prove

turns.text: We deploy on EKS with ArgoCD and Spacelift managing infrastructure. Where do your agent platform components live in that picture, and what does a rollout of a new tool version look like?
turns.expected_stems: eks argocd spacelift components rollout tool version

turns.text: Our OpenAPI spec is the contract our partners integrate against. Make the case that an agent tool layer should be generated from that spec rather than hand written, and tell me where generation breaks down.
turns.expected_stems: openapi spec contract tool layer generated hand written breaks

turns.text: A partner reports that your monitoring agent flagged a corporate action incorrectly and a customer saw a wrong dividend adjustment. Walk me through the postmortem artifacts you would already have.
turns.expected_stems: corporate action incorrectly dividend adjustment postmortem artifacts
